The ending of the story feels completely natural, earned, and purposeful. It directly resolves the central conflict introduced in the very first paragraph—Daniel's recurring dream about the unused apartment and his lingering, passive anxiety over the way his first marriage ended. By finding the physical keys to his past (both the key to his ex-wife's apartment and the locker key from a pivotal early memory with Isabel), Daniel is prompted to take active steps to break the "terrifying, familiar drift" creeping into his current relationship. The final scene on the lake ties together the story's themes of presence, partnership, and letting go of obsolete structures, culminating in Daniel's satisfying internal resolution to finally "move out" of the dream apartment and match Isabel's rhythm in the real world.
